Which sensors it came from and how many were averaged. Recorded so that the figure can be traced back later.
Leave it empty to use the computed denominator. Fill it in when the plant builds its denominator its own way under the contract.
The performance ratio the contractor commits to in the contract. Used for comparison, and as the basis for a penalty if it is not met.
The gap between the override denominator and the computed one. Anything other than 0 means there is something about the plant's formula we have not understood.
The baseline for the temperature correction. STC is 25 °C, but a contract may settle on something else — declare the contract's figure.
Once a person overrides the system's figure it switches to "taken by the system, edited by a person" — so it is still known afterwards which figure was touched.
Where a plant has 2–3 irradiance sensors, whether to average them or use only one is the customer's decision, not the software's.
The total solar energy reaching the module surface during the day. This is the DENOMINATOR of the performance ratio — get this field wrong and the whole KPI is wrong.
One record per plant per day. The fields on the left the system takes from\n               the readings; those on the right the duty operator observes by eye.
The temperature coefficient at the maximum power point — a module specification, usually negative (−0.004 means 0.4% of the power is lost per degree of extra heat).
An irradiation of %s kWh/m²/day is implausible — the highest recorded anywhere on Earth is around 9. Check the unit: this may be Wh/m² rather than kWh/m².

The constants are captured when the record is created; they are not a live reference. Editing the plant's constants today must not change a KPI already computed for last month.

Leave it empty and the module area above is used. Declare it separately when the contract uses the GROSS AREA (frames included) for the performance ratio denominator — a 2–3% difference against the light-collecting area, and that difference goes straight into the KPI.
